theory.title: Inversion and cleft sentences
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 081. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Inversion and cleft sentences
patterns.pattern: Not only + auxiliary / What ... is ...
examples: Not only did the policy reduce costs, but it also improved access.
What matters most is reliable evidence.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 081 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 081 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 082 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 083 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Past perfect and narrative tenses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 084. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Past perfect and narrative tenses
patterns.pattern: had + past participle / had been + -ing
examples: They had already discussed the issue.
She had been reflecting on the decision for weeks.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

theory.title: Wish and if only
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 085. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Wish and if only
patterns.pattern: wish / if only + past or past perfect
examples: I wish I were more patient.
If only I had asked for clarification.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 086 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 086 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Passive forms and reporting
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 087. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Passive forms and reporting
patterns.pattern: be + past participle / it is reported that
examples: The proposal was approved after consultation.
It is widely believed that early support matters.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

theory.title: Conditionals and concession
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 088. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Conditionals and concession
patterns.pattern: if / unless / provided that / although
examples: If access improves, participation will rise.
Although the plan is costly, it may be worthwhile.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 088 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Modal deduction and speculation
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 089. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Modal deduction and speculation
patterns.pattern: must / may / might / can't have + participle
examples: The figures must have been updated.
The delay might have been caused by the weather.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

phrases.english: A key issue is how decisions are justified.
phrases.spanish: Una cuestión clave es cómo se justifican las decisiones.

phrases.english: There is more to consider than first appears.
phrases.spanish: Hay más que considerar de lo que parece a primera vista.

content.passage: The question of 089 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 089 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.

theory.title: Participle clauses
theory.explanation: This mission develops the language of 090. At B2, express relationships, degrees of certainty and contrasting perspectives precisely. Use the target structure to connect ideas rather than producing isolated sentences.

patterns.label: Participle clauses
patterns.pattern: -ing / having + past participle
examples: Having considered both sides, she changed her mind.
Faced with criticism, he responded calmly.

patterns.label: Qualification
patterns.pattern: It could be argued that… / To some extent… / The evidence appears to suggest that…
examples: It could be argued that the proposal is effective in the short term.
The evidence appears to suggest that further evaluation is needed.

theory.tip: Avoid absolute claims unless the evidence justifies them. Vary sentence openings, use precise vocabulary and check that complex clauses remain easy to follow.

content.passage: The question of 090 has become increasingly relevant, particularly for people working towards more informed and responsible decisions. At the outset, the group assumed that the issue would be straightforward. A closer examination, however, revealed that recent evidence needed to be considered alongside practical experience. The review included people from different backgrounds, and participants repeatedly valued clear explanations and fair access to information. One concern was that short-term figures could be misleading if they were separated from their wider context. The team therefore compared several perspectives rather than relying on a single account. Experts recommended testing proposals locally before introducing them on a larger scale. The pilot suggested that modest adjustments could improve engagement, although the results were not identical in every setting. The report also highlighted the importance of transparent communication and clearly defined responsibilities. Its authors argued that decisions should reflect more than one perspective and should be supported by relevant evidence. Ultimately, progress in 090 depends on careful evaluation, open discussion and a willingness to revise an approach when new information becomes available.
